subject: Disputed retrocharge for prefetch deduplication
messages:
From: Arielle Jensen <arielle@scalesoft.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@scalesoft.com
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected retrocharge on August invoice — prefetched requests

Hi Dylan,

We were reviewing the August invoice and saw a $6,400 retroactive charge labeled "prefetch deduplication retrocharge". Our engineering team pulled the attached usage_export_202609.csv and we do not see matching duplicate request IDs that would justify an automated retrocharge. Can you help explain the calculation and whether this can be reversed?

This charge pushed us over the committed threshold, which impacts our renewals discussion next week. If this is an accurate charge, we need the breakdown per API key and timestamps so we can reconcile internally.

Thanks,
Arielle Jensen
Head of Platform Ops, ScaleSoft
ari.j@scalesoft.com

Attachment: usage_export_202609.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Arielle Jensen <arielle@scalesoft.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected retrocharge on August invoice — prefetched requests

Hi Arielle — thanks for the note and the export. I pulled the invoice and our retrocharge note; the short answer is we triggered a retro-billing rule after we deduped a late batch of prefetch requests that arrived with inconsistent request IDs. That dedup step runs as a backend job and when it consolidates, it can change the billing attribution which in this case created a retrocharge against your peak month.

I don't want to leave you with just that explanation. I'm looping in our billing team to provide the per-key breakdown and the exact job run logs that led to the adjustment. We should have a preliminary breakdown by EOD tomorrow.

Apologies for the disruption — I know this timing is bad with your renewal cadence.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected retrocharge on August invoice — request for per-key breakdown

Ben / Kim — forwarding Arielle's thread. ScaleSoft is disputing a $6.4k retrocharge that was applied after a dedup job consolidated prefetch requests. They ask for a per-API-key + timestamp breakdown and the job logs that explain why the retrocharge re-attributed usage to August.

Key asks:
- CSV with per-key token counts before/after dedup job (aligned to timestamps)
- The dedup job run id and the criteria we used to merge request IDs (specifically: case-insensitive hashing? request_id header vs generated uuid?)
- Whether this retrocharge can be limited to non-committed tiers (i.e., don't bump committed usage) or if we can offer a one-time credit given their renewal timing

Can you take ownership on the trace + a recommended remediation (full reversal vs partial credit)? If you need infra logs, tell me which IDs to pull and I will escalate.

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected retrocharge on August invoice — request for per-key breakdown

Dylan / Kim — I dug into the billing run and the dedup pipeline. Summary below: 

What happened:
- On 2026-08-31 23:18:14 UTC a late reprocessor run (run_id: dedup-20260831-23) consolidated ~42k prefetch records that arrived with multiple request_id variants.
- The consolidation logic normalizes the request_id header by trimming and lowercasing; however, a subset of clients (including ScaleSoft) had a client-side library bug that appended microsecond UUIDs to the end of request_id in some retries. The dedup job still consolidated them but attributed the consolidated sessions to the original received timestamps, which overlapped the August billing window and raised their peak.

What I can provide:
- Attached breakdown CSV with before/after token counts (per API key) and the dedup run id.
- A short audit log extract showing sample raw request_id values and how they mapped.

Options to resolve:
1) Full reversal of the retrocharge and reissue pro forma credit (requires finance approval; risks undercounting if we later find evidence).
2) Partial credit equal to the delta that moved them over the committed threshold (quick, lower risk).
3) Offer credit + a short engineering whitelist to prevent similar auto-dedupe retrocharges for one billing cycle while ScaleSoft fixes their client bug.

My recommendation: option 2 + temporary whitelist while they patch. It's conservative and keeps renewals on track. If you want a stronger gesture for strategic reasons we can escalate 1.

Attached: dedup_run_deltas_20260831.csv (CSV), audit_samples.txt

Ben
Senior Billing Analyst, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Arielle Jensen <arielle@scalesoft.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected retrocharge on August invoice — prefetched requests

Hi Arielle — quick update and proposed remediation. Ben ran the audit and attached a per-API-key before/after breakdown plus sample raw request_id traces. Short summary: the retro-billing came from a late dedup job that consolidated requests with slightly different request_id variants; that consolidation pushed a small delta into August peak.

Proposed next steps we can do today:
- Apply a one-time partial credit of $3,500 which covers the delta that crossed your committed tier (option 2 from below).
- Temporarily whitelist your account from auto retrocharge re-attribution for one billing cycle while your engineers ship the fix; we'll provide guidance on the exact normalization pattern that caused this.

If you'd like a full reversal we can route this to finance for an exception but it will take 4–7 business days to complete approvals.

Let me know which you prefer and I will action it immediately. Thanks for flagging this — we'll include a short postmortem to avoid repeat occurrences.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: invoice_202608.pdf (PDF, 180KB)
